title: Production and purification of recombinant monoclonal antibodies from human cells based on a primary sequence
protocol: Design and order two separate gene fragments containing the entire heavy chain sequence of the antibody.
Design and order two separate gene fragments containing the entire light chain sequence of the antibody.
Optimize the sequences using a codon optimization algorithm for expression in human cells.
Ensure that the gene fragments contain the necessary sequence elements for downstream cloning, such as appropriate overhangs for Gibson assembly.
Include signal peptide sequences in both heavy and light chain gene fragments.
Use native signal peptides if available through transcriptome sequencing.
Add signal peptide sequences N-terminal to the variable region if not present.
Order only variable regions of each chain as a cost-saving alternative.
Clone variable regions into parent plasmids with constant regions of choice.
Follow manufacturer’s protocol to suspend DNA in nuclease-free water.
Centrifuge the tube for 3–5 s at 3,000 × g in a microcentrifuge to pellet material to bottom of the tube.
Add nuclease-free water to the tube to reach the desired concentration.
Briefly vortex, and spin down again.
Determine DNA fragment concentration using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Store prepared fragments at -20°C when not in use.
Digest 1 μg of the pEGFP-N1 plasmid with appropriate restriction enzymes.
Run the digest on a 1% agarose gel in 1× TAE buffer.
Cut out the band corresponding to digested plasmid from the agarose gel using a clean razor blade.
Place the cut-out DNA band in an Eppendorf tube.
Purify the DNA from the agarose gel using a DNA gel recovery kit.
Determine the concentration of the purified DNA digest using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Use the digested plasmid for heavy and light chain “parent” plasmids as needed in downstream cloning reactions.
Store any unused parent plasmids at −20°C.
Clone entire heavy and light chain DNA from gene fragments into separate, digested heavy and light chain parent plasmids using the Gibson assembly method.
Prepare a single 15 μL aliquot of isothermal enzyme mix for the Gibson reaction.
Add 50–100 ng of digested parent plasmid to the isothermal enzyme mix.
Include gene fragment DNA in a 1:2 molar ratio relative to the parent plasmid.
For heavy chain cloning, use 100 ng parent plasmid and 70 ng heavy chain DNA fragment.
For light chain cloning, use 100 ng parent plasmid and 35 ng light chain DNA fragment.
Bring the total reaction volume to 20 μL with H2O.
Mix the Gibson assembly reaction components thoroughly.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 50°C for 20 minutes.
Transform 3 μL of each cloning reaction into DH5α competent E. coli cells.
Grow transformed cells on appropriate LB + antibiotic agar plates.
Select individual colonies from the plates.
Inoculate selected colonies in 3 mL LB plus antibiotic.
Shake at 225 rpm for 16 h at 37°C.
Purify plasmid DNA clones using a DNA miniprep kit.
Screen for correct plasmid clones by Sanger or nanopore sequencing.
Store positive clones as miniprep DNA at −20°C.
Design two separate gene fragments for the heavy chain variable sequence.
Design two separate gene fragments for the light chain variable sequence.
Include signal peptide sequences in the gene fragments.
Ensure necessary overlap sequences are included for downstream cloning.
Design primers using standard PCR methodologies for the heavy chain constant region.
Perform PCR to obtain DNA fragments of the heavy chain constant region using PCRBio VeriFi Mix or similar.
Design primers using standard PCR methodologies for the light chain constant region.
Perform PCR to obtain DNA fragments of the light chain constant region using PCRBio VeriFi Mix or similar.
To a single 15 μL aliquot of isothermal assembly enzyme mix, add 50–100 ng of digested parent plasmid.
Add the variable region gene fragment and corresponding constant region PCR fragment to the enzyme mix using a 1:2:2 molar ratio.
Assemble the heavy chain expression plasmid by mixing 100 ng of digested parent plasmid, 20 ng heavy chain variable region fragment, and 50 ng heavy chain constant region PCR fragment.
Assemble the light chain expression plasmid using the same process as for the heavy chain.
Follow steps 4b–4g to complete the cloning process.
Prepare purified DNA of the appropriate expression plasmids containing both the heavy and light chain antibody sequences.
Ensure that DNA preparations contain an endotoxin removal step.
Seed 30 mL cells at 1 × 10^6 cells/mL twenty-four hours prior to transfection for a total of 30 × 10^6 cells.
Count cells on the day of transfection and ensure viability is greater than >90%.
Centrifuge 45 × 10^6 cells at 2,000 × g for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
Gently resuspend cell pellet in 15 mL fresh Expi293F media.
Return resuspended cells to spinner flasks and incubate in an orbital shaker.
Mix 100 μL of polyethylenimine (PEI) at 1 mg/mL with 1 mL serum-free Optimem media.
In a second tube, mix 50 μg of the light chain plasmid, 35 μg of the heavy chain plasmid in 1 mL Optimem media.
Incubate contents of both tubes for 5 minutes with occasional flicking at a temperature between 20°C and 25°C.
Incubate the contents of two tubes together for 15 minutes at a temperature between 20°C–25°C.
Flick the tube approximately every 2 minutes to ensure thorough mixing during incubation.
Remove cells from the orbital shaker and add the transfection reaction mixture.
Place the cells back in the shaker and incubate for 24 hours, rotating at 125 rpm.
After 24 hours, remove cells from the shaker and add 15 mL of fresh Expi293F media to the existing culture.
Add 300 μL of 220 mM valproic acid to the mixture.
Return cells to the shaker and incubate for 4 days.
Four days after adding valproic acid, test cell media for positive antibody reactivity using an assay intended for purified antibodies.
Remove 0.5 mL of the media from the cells.
Spin at 2,000 × g for 4 minutes at 4°C to collect the supernatant/clarified media.
Test a range of dilutions of the clarified media (from undiluted to 1:1000) for antibody reactivity.
Typically test the media at days 4, 5, and 6 post-transfection to determine the optimal time window for harvesting antibodies.
Purify antibodies after determining the optimal time window.
Remove cells from the incubator four to six days post-transfection.
Transfer cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Collect the antibody-containing supernatant.
Pass the collected supernatant through a 0.2 μm filter into a sterile 100 mL glass bottle.
Measure the volume of filtered supernatant.
Add 1.0 M Tris-HCl (pH 7.4) to adjust pH between 7.4 and 7.7.
Store the adjusted supernatant at 4°C until purification, ideally within 24 hours.
Remove a prepared Protein A Sepharose column from storage at 4°C.
Attach the Protein A Sepharose column to a column stand.
Drain the storage buffer from the column.
Wash the column with 30 mL of 1 × TBS (pH 8.0).
Apply the antibody-containing cell media to the column.
Close the stopcock.
Place a funnel reservoir on top of the column.
Move the column apparatus to a 4°C cold room.
Slowly add filtered cell media to the column until it fills the column and partially fills the funnel reservoir.
Allow disrupted Protein A Sepharose to settle for 1 hour.
Place a reservoir adaptor with an inlet for tubing on the funnel reservoir.
Attach the apparatus to a peristaltic pump with tubing.
Open the stopcock.
Turn on the peristaltic pump.
Collect the flow-through at a rate of 1 mL/min into a sterile glass bottle.
Close the stopcock when liquid approaches the compacted Protein A Sepharose bed.
Remove the reservoir adaptor.
Gently add collected flow-through back to the funnel reservoir.
Allow the Protein A Sepharose to re-settle for 1 hour.
Open the stopcock again.
Collect the flow-through at a rate of 1 mL/min until liquid approaches the compacted Protein A Sepharose bed.
Close the stopcock when liquid nears the compacted bed.
Remove the funnel reservoir.
Slowly add 3 mL of 1 × TBS (pH 8.0) to the column and let it settle for 15 minutes.
Gently attach a column adaptor with a threaded valve on top of the column.
Connect via tubing to the peristaltic pump.
Open the stopcock.
Collect the flow-through at a rate of 1 mL/min.
Close the stopcock when the buffer approaches the top of the compacted Protein A Sepharose.
Elute the antibody from the Protein A Sepharose by slowly adding 9 mL of elution buffer.
Open the stopcock and set the peristaltic pump to a flow rate of 5 mL/min.
Collect the eluate in a 15 mL conical tube containing 0.9 mL 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).
Cap and invert the 15 mL conical tube immediately after all elution buffer has entered the column to mix and neutralize the solution.
Clean the Protein A Sepharose column immediately by gently filling it with elution buffer and setting the peristaltic pump to 5 mL/min.
Wash the column with two column volumes (approximately 20 mL) of elution buffer followed by two column volumes (∼20 mL) of 1 × TBS (pH 8.0).
Stop the pump when the 1 × TBS (pH 8.0) approaches the compacted Protein A Sepharose bed and close the stopcock.
Fill the column with 20% EtOH (∼7 mL), place a cap on it, and store upright at 4°C for future use.
Transfer the eluate from step 17 into a pre-soaked dialysis membrane.
Seal the dialysis membrane with dialysis clips.
Place the sealed dialysis membrane into a beaker containing 1 L of 1 × PBS (pH 7.2) and a 6 cm stir bar.
Gently stir at 4°C for 4 hours.
Replace the 1 × PBS (pH 7.2) with fresh 1 L of 1 × PBS after 4 hours.
Stir gently at 4°C for 14–16 hours.
Soak a 30 kDa cutoff centrifugal filter concentrator in 1 × PBS for 1 minute.
Spin the concentrator at 2000 x g for 1 minute to remove PBS.
Retrieve purified, dialyzed antibodies from the tubing and place into the concentrator (should be approximately 10 mL).
Spin at 2,000 × g and check the volume of the concentrated antibody solution every 20 minutes until it reaches between 100 and 200 μL.
Remove the purified antibody from the concentrator.
Measure the protein concentration using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Dilute the antibody to 1–2 mg/mL in 1 × PBS (pH 7.2) plus 15% glycerol.
Aliquot the diluted antibody into tubes for storage at −20°C.
Make small-volume aliquots of 2–5 μL and large-volume stock aliquots of 100–200 μL.
Thaw stock aliquots as needed, then re-aliquot into smaller volumes of 2–5 μL.
Serially dilute a sample of the purified antibody.
Load a 4%–12% SDS-polyacrylamide gel with the samples ranging from ∼0.01 μg to 40 μg.
Run the gel according to standard SDS-PAGE protocols.
Stain and destain the gel with Coomassie Brilliant Blue or other appropriate protein stain.
Validate antibodies for the intended application after purification, such as immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, or immunoprecipitation.
